newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-HUMILIATED PSG OPT TO TRAIN BEHIND CLOSED DOORS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HUMILIATED PSG OPT TO TRAIN BEHIND CLOSED DOORS.

text.p: Paris St Germain, chastened by Saturday's French Cup collapse at fourth division Clermont, chose on Monday to train in private for their European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final first leg at home to AEK Athens.

Club president Michel Denisot no doubt had hard words for the players, who astonishingly let slip a 4-1 lead with 22 minutes to go at Clermont, after Monday's open practice. But he would not talk to reporters afterwards.

Manager Ricardo said his squad would train behind closed doors at Clairfontaine to the south of Paris on Tuesday and Wednesday to prepare for the visit to the Parc des Princes of the Greek side on Thursday.
Ricardo said he would not resign and Denisot did not ask his Brazilian protege to do so, heaping the blame for the debacle entirely on the players.
"This time it's impossible to shield the players, they are 100 percent responsible," Denisot said on Sunday when the PSG board held an emergency meeting.
Sources close to the club said Denisot could be considering fines as punishment for a lack of professional application by the players.
But none of the players will be axed from a small squad which has been reduced further by injury to defenders Jimmy Algerino, Alain Roche and Didier Domi.
Misunderstandings in defence have become commonplace in PSG's recent matches.
Goalkeeper Bernard Lama, who looked sharp playing for France last week, conceded two crucial goals in a week due to mix-ups with PSG team mates.
In PSG's last league match at home, Guingamp's Stephane Carnot scored direct from a corner when Lama and Benoit Cauet failed to agree on who should clear the ball at the near post.

Against Clermont, who had just five shots on target, it was Bruno N'Gotty who misread Lama's intentions and gave the fourth division side an equaliser with an own goal which made the score at 4-4 and sent the tie to penalties.
Clermont goalkeeper Olivier Enjolras then saved the spot kicks of PSG veterans Paul Le Guen and Vincent Guerin, who visibly wilted under the responsibility.
N'Gotty, anticipating wholesale changes in the close season, said: "We're in a bad way. We've still got three, four months to live together. We must do it to the full."
The only important difference Ricardo can bring to his side is the return of mercurial midfielder Leonardo, who was rested on Saturday after playing for Brazil in Gioania in midweek.

If the holders are to hang on to their trophy, Leonardo must play as he did against Galatasaray in the previous round when he inspired PSG to a 4-0 home win after they had lost the away leg 4-2 without him.

But they were in better shape then. This year they have fallen well behind Monaco in the French league title race, have been eliminated from both domestic cups and shipped nine Juventus goals over two legs of the European Super Cup.
